screening_decisions.reason: Randomized clinical study comparing biocompatible (polyacrylonitrile) vs bioincompatible (cuprophane) membranes in 72 ARF patients requiring hemodialysis. Meets all selection criteria.
Observational study about hemodialysis complications and renal recovery. No comparison of BCM vs BICM membranes. Not an RCT.
Prospective observational multicentre study assessing prognostic factors. While it mentions membrane comparison, this is not a randomized controlled trial comparing BCM vs BICM.
Prospective randomized study comparing bioincompatible (cuprophane) vs biocompatible (polyacrylonitrile) membranes in 52 ARF patients requiring hemodialysis. Meets all selection criteria.
Study about hemofiltration, not intermittent hemodialysis. Compares high-permeability vs conventional hemofiltration membranes, not BCM vs BICM comparison as defined in criteria.
Meta-analysis about myocardial infarction treatments. Wrong topic - not about ARF or dialysis membranes.
Study about hemofiltration, not intermittent hemodialysis. Wrong intervention modality per selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial comparing cellulose acetate (substituted cellulose) vs polysulfone (synthetic) membranes in 66 ARF patients requiring intermittent hemodialysis. Meets selection criteria.
Meta-analysis of existing trials, not a primary randomized controlled trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
Methodological paper about meta-analysis inconsistency measurement. Not a clinical trial about ARF or dialysis membranes.

Comparative study of biocompatible vs bioincompatible membranes in 57 ARF patients requiring hemodialysis. While randomization not explicitly stated, appears to be a controlled comparison meeting the intervention criteria. Conservative inclusion.
Observational prognostic study using regression analysis. No comparison of dialysis membranes. Not an RCT.
Compares two synthetic membranes (both biocompatible), not BCM vs BICM. Also uses continuous venovenous dialysis, not intermittent hemodialysis as required by criteria.
Review article summarizing published clinical trials. Not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Paper discussing discordant meta-analyses. Not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Abstract appears corrupted with unrelated rat study references. Cannot verify if this is an RCT comparing BCM vs BICM in ARF patients. Excluded due to inability to assess eligibility.
Study about publication bias in oncology trials. Wrong topic - not about ARF or dialysis membranes.
Review about dialysate purity and ultrapure dialysate. Not a randomized trial comparing BCM vs BICM membranes.
Study about pretransplantation hemodialysis in kidney transplant patients. Wrong population - not ARF patients requiring hemodialysis, but transplant candidates.
Observational registry study analyzing risk factors for survival in ARF. No comparison of BCM vs BICM membranes. Not an RCT.
Review article summarizing existing clinical trials, not a primary randomized controlled trial.

Crossover study comparing cellulose acetate vs polysulfone (both relatively biocompatible). Primary outcomes are cellular responses (cytokine synthesis, superoxide release, neutrophil apoptosis), not survival or renal function recovery.

Prospective randomized controlled trial comparing cellulose diacetate (modified cellulose with lower complement activation) vs polysulfone (synthetic biocompatible membrane) in 159 ARF patients requiring HD. Outcomes include survival and time to recover renal function.
Review article discussing concepts of dialysis membrane biocompatibility and summarizing clinical studies, not a primary randomized controlled trial.

Randomized trial comparing low-flux polysulfone vs high-flux polyacrylonitrile. Both are synthetic biocompatible membranes; the comparison is about flux characteristics, not biocompatibility (BCM vs BICM).
Observational cohort study using USRDS data. Population consists of chronic hemodialysis patients (dialysis for at least 1 year), not acute renal failure patients. Not a randomized trial.

Prospective randomized multicentre trial comparing bioincompatible Cuprophan vs biocompatible polymethyl-methacrylate membranes in 180 dialysis-dependent ARF patients. Primary outcome is survival 14 days after end of therapy.
Meta-analysis of randomized trials evaluating ACE inhibitors for nondiabetic renal disease. Does not address dialysis membrane biocompatibility.
Review article examining developments in renal replacement therapies, not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Randomized trial comparing extended daily dialysis vs continuous hemodialysis modalities. Does not compare biocompatible vs bioincompatible membranes.

Prospective multicenter quasi-randomized trial (alternating order assignment) comparing biocompatible membranes (low complement activation) vs bioincompatible cellulosic membranes (high complement activation) in 153 ARF patients. Outcomes include survival and recovery of renal function.

Retrospective analysis of observational data from French Prospective Multicenter Study. Membrane type was not assigned by protocol ('centers followed their usual practice'), so not a randomized or quasi-randomized trial.

Randomized trial comparing high-permeability vs conventional haemofiltration using polyamide membranes with different cut-off points. Both membranes are similar materials; comparison is about pore size/permeability not biocompatibility. Uses continuous haemofiltration, not intermittent hemodialysis. Outcomes are PBMC proliferation, not survival or renal recovery.
Expert discussion/debate article about pathophysiology of ARF, not a primary randomized controlled trial.
